description:
Measured 2026-09-14 at main f26264572 with a probe that runs count(100000, 0) and prints Process.heap_alloc_stats(): reductions_executed is 400000 on fz2 run and 0 on fz2 interp; on quicksort, reductions_remaining is 4000 (the untouched quantum) on interp and 3906 on run. The cooperative back-edge yield check is emitted by native codegen only (src/compiler2/native_codegen/terminator.rs:1136-1157); the interpreter calls reset_reduction_budget (ir_interp/backend.rs:456) and never decrements.

Consequence: three-path parity is broken for scheduling. An interpreted process that loops without a mailbox barrier runs until it finishes; any fixture that depends on fair interleaving between processes passes on interp for a different reason than on run and build, and the reductions counters cannot be used as an interpreter signal.

Fix: the interpreter charges a reduction at the same points the native doors do (call and back edge) and yields on the same budget. Signal: the probe above prints equal reductions_executed on all three doors; a two-process fairness fixture with a spinning producer and a consumer that must be scheduled, pinned by output order on three doors.
title: The interpreter never spends reductions, so an interpreted process is never preempted
